data.description:
# Gym index scene

## Problem statement

The project now has multiple gym scenes (player movement + enemy testbeds) but no way to reach them: `gameConfig.ts` hard-codes a single scene, so each scene can only be tested by editing source. Developers need a gym entry page that automatically lists every available gym scene, booted first in dev mode, so individual scenes can be selected and tested in isolation without touching code.

## Users

- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — want to boot the project, see every gym scene listed, click one to test it in isolation, and return to the list; adding a new gym scene must not require editing the index.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want to start the app with `npm run dev` (or `npm run preview`) and land on a gym index that lists all gym scenes sorted alphabetically, so I can pick what to test.
- As a **developer**, I want the scene list to be discovered from `src/scenes/gym/` rather than hard-coded, so a newly added `GymDiver.ts` appears automatically without editing the index.
- As a **developer**, I want entries labelled from their filename (e.g. `Scout`, `Tank`, `Player`) and, on selection, to jump straight into that scene.
- As a **developer**, I want a "← INDEX" button in every gym scene so I can return to the index without reloading the page.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Player gym scene relocated & renamed:** `src/scenes/Gym.ts` (class `GymScene`) moves to `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` as class `GymPlayer` (key `GymPlayer`), consistent with the `GymScout` / `GymTank` convention; all references (game config, tests, docs) are updated and the build/typecheck passes.
- [ ] **AC2 — Gym index entry scene:** A new `GymIndex` scene is the sole scene registered in `gameConfig.ts`; running `npm run dev` or `npm run preview` boots into the index, which shows a title and the alphabetical list of discovered gym scenes.
- [ ] **AC3 — Directory-dynamic discovery (no hard-coded list):** The index enumerates gym scenes by reading `src/scenes/gym/` via Vite's `import.meta.glob` — no explicit scene array. `.test.ts` files are excluded from the list, and the index itself is not listed (it lives outside the glob folder). Adding a new `Gym<Name>.ts` file to the folder makes it appear without editing the index.
- [ ] **AC4 — Display names, sorting & immediate switching:** Labels are the filename with the leading `Gym` stripped (`GymScout` → `Scout`, `GymPlayer` → `Player`) and sorted alphabetically; selecting an entry immediately starts that scene using its class-name key.
- [ ] **AC5 — Back-to-index button:** Every gym scene (existing `GymScout` / `GymTank` updated, `GymPlayer` included, convention documented for future scenes) shows a small "← INDEX" button that switches back to `GymIndex`.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover discovery filtering (`.test.ts` excluded), display-name derivation, alphabetical sorting, and scene switching; player-scene tests are updated for the rename; full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (dev-run instructions + "adding a new gym scene" convention), and the GDD layout notes.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript + Vite (already pinned in `package.json`). Discovery must use Vite's `import.meta.glob` (works in dev server, `vite preview`, and Vitest) — browsers cannot read the filesystem at runtime.
- **Discovery is data-driven:** the index enumerates scenes from the folder contents; no scene-registry edit is required when a gym scene is added.
- **Dev-mode entry:** the index is the entry page when the server runs via `npm run dev` / `npm run preview`, per the operator. No production game scene exists yet, so the index is the single entry point for all run modes at this stage.
- **Naming conventions:** gym scenes live in `src/scenes/gym/` as `Gym<Name>.ts` with class/key `Gym<Name>`; labels strip the `Gym` prefix; the index scene lives outside the folder (e.g. `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`) so it is naturally excluded from discovery.
- **Aesthetic:** neon-vector, dark background, monospace UI text in the index (consistent with the existing gym HUD buttons — see `GymScout.ts` label style and GDD §7.1 / §2.3).
- **Back-to-index:** implemented once as a shared helper and applied to all gym scenes (existing and new), keeping scenes consistent.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/Gym.ts` — player movement gym scene, class/key `GymScene`; registered in `gameConfig.ts` as the only scene.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) and `GymScout`/`GymTank` — enemy gym scenes with in-scene HUD buttons (`EXPLODE`, `SHOOT: ON/OFF`), monospace text style.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.ts` etc. do not currently know about the index; there is no navigation between scenes.
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — `scene: [GymScene]`.
- `src/main.ts` → `core/Game.ts` → `buildGameConfig()` — the boot path.
- GDD §6.4 proposes `src/ui/Menu.ts` ("Main menu, game-over screen") for the shipped game — distinct from this dev-only gym index.
- `README.md` documents the first gym-scene intake as the implementation start; no gym-index documentation yet.

## Desired change

1. Move and rename the player gym scene: `src/scenes/Gym.ts` → `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts`, class/key `GymScene` → `GymPlayer`; update `gameConfig.ts`, tests, and any references.
2. Add `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — entry scene that discovers gym scenes from `src/scenes/gym/` via `import.meta.glob`, filters `.test.ts` files, derives labels (strip `Gym`), sorts alphabetically, and lists them as clickable entries.
3. Register `GymIndex` in `gameConfig.ts` as the entry scene so `npm run dev` / `npm run preview` boot into it.
4. Selecting an entry immediately starts that scene by its class-name key (`this.scene.start('Gym<Name>')`).
5. Add a shared "← INDEX" back-button helper and apply it to `GymScout`, `GymTank`, and `GymPlayer`.
6. Document the convention in README/GDD and unit-test the discovery/derivation/sort/switching logic.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — NEW: index/entry scene (title, discovered scene list, immediate switching).
- `src/scenes/gym/discovery.ts` (or `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`) — NEW: Vite `import.meta.glob` discovery, `.test.ts` filtering, display-name derivation, alphabetical sort; pure, unit-testable.
- `src/utils/gymNavigation.ts` — NEW: shared "← INDEX" back-button helper used by all gym scenes.
- `src/scenes/Gym.ts` → moved to `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — renamed player gym scene (class/key `GymPlayer`).
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — register `GymIndex` as the entry scene (replacing `GymScene`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts` — add the shared back-to-index button.
- `src/scenes/gym/*.test.ts`, `src/core/Game.test.ts` — updated/extended tests (rename fallout + discovery/navigation coverage).
- `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` — dev-run instructions, new-gym-scene convention, layout notes.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — index UI styling constants if shared (e.g. index colours/spacing).

## Related work

- **Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement (AH-0MT97BW7M0056S8S)** — the player gym scene being moved/renamed here.
- **Create Enemy Gym Scene work items (AH-0MT987VA3005YBNK)** — parent epic for the enemy gym scenes listed by this index.
- **Create E1 Scout gym scene (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q)** and **Create E3 Tank gym scene (AH-0MT99I2OC0014MNZ)** — completed enemy scenes that receive the back-to-index button. The original description's dependency ("dependent upon the completion of the first enemy scene") is **satisfied** — E1 Scout is completed.
- **Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9)** — related; may touch the same shared-helper area; keep the back-button helper in a neutral `src/utils/` location.
- **Bootstrap Phaser + TypeScript project scaffold (AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW)** — provides Vite, TypeScript, Vitest (dependency of all scenes).
- **Game Design Document for AI_Hell (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — authoritative spec; §6.4 layout notes updated.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — rename target:** "rename for consistency" means `GymPlayer.ts` / class+key `GymPlayer` (matching `GymScout`/`GymTank`); display label "Player". If a different name is preferred it is a mechanical rename.
- **Assumption — index location outside the glob folder** (e.g. `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`): avoids a hard-coded self-exclusion rule; everything in `src/scenes/gym/` is a listable gym scene.
- **Assumption — dev-mode equivalence:** `npm run dev` and `npm run preview` both run the same built bundle/config, so the index is the entry in both; "dev mode" is not a separate runtime flag at this stage.
- **Risk — `import.meta.glob` is build-time:** newly added files are picked up when the glob module is resolved (dev-server restart/HMR or rebuild); not a runtime directory scan. Acceptable for a dev tool — document the expectation.
- **Risk — rename fallout:** moving/renaming the player scene touches `gameConfig.ts`, tests, and GDD references; `tsc --noEmit` and the full Vitest suite are the safety net.
- **Risk — cross-cutting back button:** adding the button to existing scenes touches files owned by other work items (E1/E3 scenes); keep the change minimal (single shared helper + one button per scene) and coordinate with the Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes item.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no game menu, no pause, no per-scene config UI, no URL deep-linking, no search/filter, no thumbnails, no auto-demo mode. Anything beyond a list + immediate switching + back button is out of scope; record extras as linked work items.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the index list the player gym scene separately or only scenes in `src/scenes/gym/`? How are labels/navigation handled?" — Answer (user): "The scene should not hard code the available scenes; they should be discovered by reading the source directory for gym scenes; present them sorted alphabetically." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q2: "How should 'dev mode' be enabled — URL param, config flag, or always?" — Answer (user): "The server is started with `npm run dev` or `npm run preview` as opposed to a build." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q3: "When an entry is selected, should it switch immediately or show confirmation?" — Answer (user): "Immediately switch." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q4: "Should the player gym scene (`src/scenes/Gym.ts`) also be listed, and how are labels derived?" — Answer (user): "Move it into `src/scenes/gym/` and rename it for consistency. Labels: raw class filename, but strip `Gym` from the start. Scene key: class name is fine." Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Q5: "How should users return to the index from a gym scene?" — Answer (user): "Index button" (a small "← INDEX" button in each gym scene). Source: interactive reply (round 3).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5** – Game Design Document for AI_Hell (completed)
- **AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR** – Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model in GDD (completed)
- **AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V** – Add a Magnet power up (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: completion, create, dependent, dev, enemy, entry, first, game, gym, index, item, mode, page, run, scene, scenes, should, when, work
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: create, dev, enemy, entry, first, game, item, mode, run, scene, scenes, should, when, work

data.description:
Gym scene sliders bound to live ship config

## Goal

AC1/AC2/AC4 of parent AH-0MT9FS3DL0084Z6V: show a slider per ship config value in the gym scene; changing a slider updates the ship live.

## Design decision (operator approved proceeding without further questions)

Plain DOM control panel (not Phaser UI objects): an HTML panel next to/above the canvas so tests can assert via document.querySelector in happy-dom. The GymScene builds it in create(), reading initial values from loadShipConfig().

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Sliders rendered:** The gym scene renders one slider per numeric config value: thrustAcceleration, maxSpeed, shipSize, thrustFlameLength (input type=range with min/max/step + a live value label).
- [ ] **AC2 — Colour inputs:** shipColor, thrustFlameColor, thrustFlameInnerColor rendered as HTML color inputs (sliders are awkward for colours; still saveable).
- [ ] **AC3 — Live update:** Moving any slider/color input calls player.setConfig(...) with the merged ShipConfig immediately; physics and rendering update without restart.
- [ ] **AC4 — Initial values from config:** On scene create, controls are populated from loadShipConfig() (saved values or defaults).
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests:** happy-dom tests assert the panel renders, a slider change updates the player config (physics effect), and initial values reflect loaded config.

## Key Files

- src/scenes/Gym.ts
- src/entities/Player.ts (setConfig already exists)
- src/core/config.ts (loadShipConfig)
- index.html (container styling if needed)
